title: Children of the Whales
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Chakuro is the archivist of the Mud Whale, an exiled island-ship drifting on a sea of sand, where the emotion-powered 'Marked' die young and the 'Unmarked' rule. When he finds Lykos, an emotionless girl from outside, the ship is attacked by the Allied Empire, which sees emotion as the cause of war, and the islanders must fight to survive (Wikipedia; ANN; Viz blurb via AniList).
life_message: Feeling fully, grief included, and choosing to live together freely is worth more than a safe life without emotion.

content.note: Invading soldiers massacre villagers; a sadistic enemy enjoys killing; friends die (Wikipedia; ANN 'violent invasion'; MU Mass Murder, Genocide).
Reviewers call it 'deceptively dark' and 'progressively darker' (ANN); AniList Tragedy 70.
Gentle crushes; a farewell kiss from a spirit (Wikipedia); MangaDex safe.
Grief, ritual suppression of emotion and short lifespans (ANN; Wikipedia; MU Limited Lifespan).

dominant: Emotion versus control; mortality and memory; resisting an empire

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Fighting is defensive survival, not personal honor (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: The rule-breaking Moles and Chakuro question the elders (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty is to the whole Mud Whale community.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Rituals suppress emotion; truth about the past is uncovered (ANN).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Emotion and expression valued over the Empire's emotionless order (ANN).

folkways.japan: A shoujo fantasy with a reflective, archival narrator, echoing Japanese mono no aware, the gentle sadness of transient life.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers worry it may 'go the predictable route' of endorsing unrestrained emotion; another praises its restraint.

personified.ideology: emotion is dangerous and must be surrendered

delivery.note: The emotionless view is voiced by a converted heroine and by a sadistic enemy, so it gets both a human face and a cruel one.

winners_losers: The Mud Whale's people survive and learn their history; the Empire's emotionless order is resisted. Sympathy goes to those who feel.
to_verify: Ending and how the war resolves (series complete in 23 volumes; reviews opened cover volume 1)
